searchText: Zoom link - call in 10! https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/91725886939?pwd=b2kzT0JGeFAzTmhyb1BYSTgrZ0xwdz09 Is there a link to live notes? <@552133098075193354> There are no live notes, but after the call <@573787335796326400> typically shares a summary Indeedy. And here it is: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/BJjamMl69 WTF? I just clicked "leave meeting" It's quick and dirty - you may find a few inaccuracies as it is sometimes hard to follow all the details. The call recording is the ultimate source of truth. But people are free to edit anything I got blatantly wrong. In the capella consensus spec it seems like the process of triggering a withdrawal is not specified (it is possible that I'm blind as well) but the processing of withdrawals is. can anybody point me to the spec for triggering withdrawals? Full withdrawals happen when the validator hits the withdrawable state. Moving a validator from active to withdrawable requires a voluntary exit, which is in the phase 0 spec. ty for the quick response! so can validators enter the withdrawal queue now, it will just be delayed till withdrawals are live? are contract triggered withdrawals in any spec yet? seems like a needed powerful primitive for liquid staking protocols and staking providers. Validators can exit now if they want (and a few have done, for one reason or another). There is nothing in the specs for contract-triggered withdrawals; they would require a fair amount of changes to work. Once a validator is exited it sits in withdrawable state until capella is implemented. what does it take to get contract triggered withdrawals implemented? also, are there any plans to bring the beacon chain state to the execution layer, like the validator merkle root or the balance merkle root or previous beaconchain state roots? The validator would need to have some sort of identifier to know that withdrawals could be triggered by a given contract, and the contract's events would need to be passed over to the beacon chain. Unlikely to be worth the effort, given that withdrawal address can be a smart contract. There are plans to make the beacon state root available on the execution chain, but I don't think they have reached as far as having any sort of spec. If the contract makes a transaction to a cannonical "withdrawal contract" the passing over of events could be similar in implementation to deposits. Not super knowledgable about all the integration tho, probably ignorant. The withdrawal address being a smart contract is far less powerful than having execution layer triggered withdrawals imo. on the second point, what does it take to draft up specs and get agreement on inclusion on these sorts of features that various people are excited about? Generally, someone writes up the spec (either an EIP or a PR to the consensus specs) and gains enough support for it to be included. kk haha. maybe ill try my hand. any recommendations? Whats the default ttd of the cl again? (for exchangetransitionconfig) 2^256 - 2^10

excerpts.author: bbuddha.xyz
excerpts.content: In the capella consensus spec it seems like the process of triggering a withdrawal is not specified (it is possible that I'm blind as well) but the processing of withdrawals is. can anybody point me to the spec for triggering withdrawals?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Full withdrawals happen when the validator hits the withdrawable state.  Moving a validator from active to withdrawable requires a voluntary exit, which is in the phase 0 spec.

excerpts.author: bbuddha.xyz
excerpts.content: ty for the quick response! so can validators enter the withdrawal queue now, it will just be delayed till withdrawals are live? are contract triggered withdrawals in any spec yet? seems like a needed powerful primitive for liquid staking protocols and staking providers.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Validators can exit now if they want (and a few have done, for one reason or another).  There is nothing in the specs for contract-triggered withdrawals; they would require a fair amount of changes to work.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Once a validator is exited it sits in withdrawable state until capella is implemented.

excerpts.author: bbuddha.xyz
excerpts.content: what does it take to get contract triggered withdrawals implemented? also, are there any plans to bring the beacon chain state to the execution layer, like the validator merkle root or the balance merkle root or previous beaconchain state roots?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
The validator would need to have some sort of identifier to know that withdrawals could be triggered by a given contract, and the contract's events would need to be passed over to the beacon chain.  Unlikely to be worth the effort, given that withdrawal address can be a smart contract.

There are plans to make the beacon state root available on the execution chain, but I don't think they have reached as far as having any sort of spec.

If the contract makes a transaction to a cannonical "withdrawal contract" the passing over of events could be similar in implementation to deposits. Not super knowledgable about all the integration tho, probably ignorant. The withdrawal address being a smart contract is far less powerful than having execution layer triggered withdrawals imo.

on the second point, what does it take to draft up specs and get agreement on inclusion on these sorts of features that various people are excited about?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Generally, someone writes up the spec (either an EIP or a PR to the consensus specs) and gains enough support for it to be included.
